composition.title: Jung's Aion — Self, Christ/Antichrist, Fishes, Alchemy, and the Historical Shadow

scenes.title: Ego, shadow, and the image of perfection
The fishes give the age its temporal image
The fish is caught, worked, and made to transform
The quaternio — Anthropos, Shadow, Physis, lapis
The age becomes visible as an age

expression:return-of-zero:roz-mytheme-na.title: the ego — centre of reference, rooted beyond what it knows of itself
the shadow — recognised through moral effort; projection returning the rejected face
the Christ-image — the Self given a human face; exclusively luminous, not all the opposites
Antichrist — the compensatory counter-image within the same aeon
Pisces — the two fishes of the age, head to tail
the precessional spring-point — expectation as a historical actor
the Pistis Sophia double — bound, released, embraced, one
Leviathan split against itself, then food for the devout (chs. IX)
Epiphanius's rite — the image carried up and returned below; a pagan rite used as testimony
the round sea creature — bonesless, heated with sea water until it shines
the eyewash — the preparation becoming the capacity to see
the Echeneis — the small fish that halts ships; the magnet taught to attract it
Mercurius — substance and philosophy; the lapis within darkness
the aftermath — science born, the mother receding as outlived; the investigating psyche disappearing from the account
A — Anthropos
B — Shadow (the inserted modern reconstruction)
C — Physis / serpent
D — lapis
the connected diamonds — each whole unfolding into four and passing onward (p.259)
the ring returning through differentiation — an unconscious totality becoming conscious
de-monopolisation — the inherited image becoming revisable
generative succession · historical succession — what a work makes possible vs how its image becomes an inherited condition
the register decision — Christ/Antichrist at the occupied slash, after the native derivation (Q27 §6)
